text:
bob-acme: Hey team — upgrading to the new Go SDK release is breaking our build. We get: 

go: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@v2.0.0: parsing go.mod: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/v2
        but was required as: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go

This is in CI (GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org). Any quick fix?

alice-support: Sorry about that — can you paste your project go.mod and the command you ran?

bob-acme: Sure — here's the minimal repro:

Command: `go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@v2.0.0`

project go.mod:
```
module github.com/acme/product

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go v2.0.0
)
```

This fails in CI but on my dev machine `go env GOPROXY` is the same.

carla-sdk: That error indicates a module path vs tag mismatch. For a v2+ release the module path must include the /v2 suffix (module github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/v2). If the tag is v2.0.0 but the module path in go.mod is still the v1 path, `go get` will complain.

dylan-releases: Oof — I think our release script forgot to update module path for the v2 branch when we cut the tag. The tag v2.0.0 is present but go.mod was left as `module github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go` (no /v2). That triggers exactly this error.

bob-acme: Any workaround until you push a fix? We need CI passing today.

carla-sdk: Two short workarounds:
1) Use a replace in your project go.mod pointing to the v2 module locally or to a commit:
```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go => github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go v0.0.0-20260101000000-abcdef123456
```
But that's ugly and brittle.

2) Temporary `go get` the module by commit (bypasses semver tag):
`go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@abcdef123456`
This should fetch the code but may still need you to adjust imports if module path changed.

carla-sdk: Also, if you can set `GOPRIVATE` to include github.com/redwood-inference, sometimes proxy caching surfaces weirdness — but that's not the core problem here.

dylan-releases: We're going to retag a corrected release. Plan: add a fix that sets `module github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go/v2` in go.mod (and ensure go.mod + tag are consistent), push v2.0.1. ETA ~2 hours.

bob-acme: Great, that would be ideal. Will you post here once the tag is live?

carla-sdk: Yes. In the meantime, if you need to unblock CI faster, try `go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@v2.0.0` with `GOPROXY=direct` (bypass proxy) — sometimes proxy.golang.org caches older metadata. But note: because of the mismatch, it might still fail. The safest temp is the commit-based `go get` I mentioned.

dylan-releases: FYI deploy-bot just recorded the release pipeline attempt.

deploy-bot: Release pipeline run #842: tagging step failed — missing module path check.

dylan-releases: I've pushed a branch with the fix and built a candidate tag v2.0.1rc1. If you want to test: `go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@v2.0.1-rc1` (public repo).

bob-acme: Tried rc1 — works! `go get` succeeds and CI passes locally. Thanks.

alice-support: Awesome. We'll follow up to ensure we cut v2.0.1 stable and update the SDK docs/examples to mention module path and semver v2 migration notes.

carla-sdk: Postmortem item: add a release checklist step to verify `module` line in go.mod matches major tag. I'll add CI check.

dylan-releases: I'll cut v2.0.1 stable in ~1h and post here.

bob-acme: Thanks all :thumbsup: Appreciate the quick turnaround.
